transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What has been bothering you lately that made you decide to come in today?

I guess the main thing is I get pulled off track really easily. Like, I’ll be trying to finish a dashboard, and then one Slack notification comes in, or I hear a song lyric, or I suddenly think of some other project idea, and I just lose the thread of what I was doing. It’s been frustrating enough that I thought I should talk to someone.
Thinking back to when you were a kid, do you remember having similar problems staying focused or getting easily distracted back then?

Yeah, I think so. Even in elementary school, teachers would write comments like I rushed through worksheets or didn’t follow all the directions. I also remember getting in trouble for talking over other kids during group work.

At home, my parents had to sit next to me when I did homework because if they didn’t, I’d get up, wander off, or start doing something else before I finished.
How much are these problems with getting pulled off track affecting your performance at work right now—for example, are they causing missed deadlines, errors, or negative feedback from your manager?

I’m not working a regular job right now, but it has affected freelance and project stuff. I’ve lost a couple of small freelance contracts because I didn’t follow through cleanly or missed pieces people were counting on. I also missed out on a portfolio competition because I couldn’t get things together reliably.

And socially, some friends or collaborators are more hesitant to work with me now, even if they like my ideas, because they’re not sure I’ll actually finish my part.
These days, do you often feel an inner sense of restlessness, like you’re driven by a motor or can’t relax and sit still for long, even when you want to?

Yeah, I do. It’s not always super obvious, but if I have to sit through a long Zoom call or work quietly in the same spot for a while, I start feeling this uncomfortable pressure, like I need to get up and pace or at least be doing something with my hands. It’s hard to just sit still and relax.
Do you often feel a lot of nervousness or worry in your day-to-day life, even when nothing in particular is going wrong at that moment?
I don’t think so, not in a constant way. I mean, I get nervous about specific things sometimes, like anyone, but I haven’t really noticed myself worrying a lot when nothing is actually going on.
Do you have ongoing trouble falling asleep at night, like your mind won’t shut off and you regularly lie awake much longer than you’d like before actually drifting off?
I’m not really sure. I don’t think that’s a major thing for me. Sometimes it takes me a bit to settle, but I haven’t noticed regularly lying awake for a long time because my mind won’t shut off.

When you think about conversations or social situations, do you often find it hard to read other people’s cues—like knowing when it’s your turn to talk, whether they’re bored, or what they’re feeling from their tone or expressions?

I don’t think that’s something I really struggle with. I can usually tell when someone wants to talk or if they’re getting bored. Maybe I miss things occasionally, but not in a way I’ve really noticed as a pattern.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you often felt noticeably down, sad, or like you’ve lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?
Not really, no. I mean, I have normal off days, but over the last couple weeks I haven’t felt noticeably sad or lost interest in things I usually like.

In your day-to-day life right now, outside of work—like managing bills, chores, appointments, or personal projects—do your focus and follow-through problems cause you to miss or forget important things often enough that it creates real problems for you?

Yeah, it does sometimes cause problems. I forget basic things unless I put in a bunch of reminders—like returning a call, sending a follow-up email, or bringing my sketchbook when I’m meeting people. And even with reminders, I’ll sometimes just swipe them away thinking I’ll do it in a minute, and then I forget again.

Back in grade school and high school, did your trouble with focus and getting distracted show up in at least two different places—for example both at school and at home—rather than just in one setting?

Yeah, it was definitely in more than one place. At school, even in elementary school, teachers would write comments about me rushing through worksheets or losing track of directions. I’d also talk over other kids during group work sometimes.

And at home, my parents had to sit with me during homework because I’d get up, wander off, or start doing something else before I finished. So it wasn’t just a school thing.
